correctness.rationale: Kaneko–Stoll Thm. 2.2 assumes both factor weights at least two, their maximum at least three, odd positive factors, and product weight three. The proof text should retain the first condition when paraphrasing the general theorem, but the actual 3,3 application satisfies it and gives the strict global cutoff 2^23. Every admissible product and factor is then of the form 1+2^i+2^j with 1≤i<j≤22. The independent integer replay `python3 /workspace/replay_binary_weight_3.py` built the 231-element set, excluded a>sqrt(2^23−1), bounded b by floor((2^23−1)/a), and tested all 3672 remaining unordered pairs including equal factors. Membership in the set returned precisely (7,7,49), (7,19,133), (7,37,259), (11,35,385), (13,21,273), (21,49,1029). Thus 1029 is the unique maximum. Exhaustion relies on the inspected published theorem, not on a finite search alone.
